data.current_summary: Remote MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP transport, JSON-RPC 2.0, stateless)
data.current_description: Tools: verify_text, normalize_allele, allele_info, match_score, check_typing, donor_compat, validate_gl_string, beta_signup, research_access, about. Every tool call but about, beta_signup and research_access consumes one call of the caller's daily quota, the same one /v1/* spends. donor_compat is decision support only; not a medical device. beta_signup and research_access are the only tools that write. Same input rule as REST: send allele names, typing strings, GL strings and HLA report text, never patient identifiers. See the MCP for agents section above.
data.summary_suggestion: Execute HLA verification tools via JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP protocol
data.description_suggestion: Stateless Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint for AI agents to invoke HLA nomenclature and matching tools via JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP. Available tools: verify_text, normalize_allele, allele_info, match_score, check_typing, donor_compat, validate_gl_string, beta_signup, research_access, and about. Quota consumption: all tools except about, beta_signup, and research_access consume one daily quota call (same quota as REST /v1/* endpoints). Input requirements: send only allele names, typing strings, GL strings, and HLA report text—never send patient identifiers (names, MRNs, DOB, accession numbers, case IDs). Limitations: donor_compat is decision support only and not a medical device; beta_signup and research_access are the only write operations. Returns JSON-RPC 2.0 responses with tool results or errors.

data.current_summary: Normalize reported typings to the current release
data.current_description: maxItems is the ceiling. The cap that applies to a request is the caller's tier's (free 250, starter 250, lab 5,000, scale 5,000, enterprise 5,000, academic 5,000), reported on every response as x-hla-verify-max-typings; a batch over it is a 422 naming the cap and the tier that lifts it.
data.description_suggestion: Converts reported HLA allele names and typing strings to current IPD-IMGT/HLA nomenclature. Accepts up to 4 alleles per locus in various formats: current names, legacy spellings (A*0101, Cw*07:02), deleted names, G/P group names, XX codes, and GL strings. Returns normalized allele names mapped to the pinned release. Batch size is limited by tier (free/starter 250, lab/scale/academic 5,000, enterprise uncapped); requests exceeding the tier limit return 422 with the applicable cap. Every response includes x-hla-verify-max-typings header indicating the tier's batch ceiling.

data.current_summary: Normalize reported typings to the current release
data.current_description: maxItems is the ceiling. The cap that applies to a request is the caller's tier's (free 250, starter 250, lab 5,000, scale 5,000, enterprise 5,000, academic 5,000), reported on every response as x-hla-verify-max-typings; a batch over it is a 422 naming the cap and the tier that lifts it.
data.description_suggestion: Converts reported HLA allele names and typing strings to current IPD-IMGT/HLA nomenclature. Accepts up to 4 alleles per locus in various formats: current names, legacy spellings (A*0101, Cw*07:02), deleted names, G/P group names, XX codes, and GL strings. Returns normalized allele names mapped to the pinned release. Batch size is limited by tier (free/starter 250, lab/scale/academic 5,000, enterprise uncapped); requests exceeding the tier limit return 422 with the applicable cap. Every response includes x-hla-verify-max-typings header indicating the tier's batch ceiling.
